accident_report:
(Initialization)
On a single-direction roadway with four lanes and a wide shoulder on the right, the road is flat but includes a gentle left-hand curve ahead. The pavement is wet, although visibility remains good. Vehicle V1 is traveling in lane 2 at 95 km/h, maintaining a steady course with the intention of continuing straight through the curve. Behind V1, Vehicle V2 is in the same lane at 105 km/h, following at a short distance of approximately 8 meters, intending to maintain speed and overtake later. In lane 3 to the left of V1, Vehicle V3 is slightly ahead of V1, traveling at 70 km/h, moving steadily but at a significantly lower speed. On the far right, in lane 1 near the wide shoulder, Vehicle V4 is traveling at 90 km/h, maintaining a stable trajectory and intending to continue forward without lane changes.

(Scenario Development)
As the vehicles approach the curve, the wet road surface reduces tire-road friction. V2, already following V1 too closely, begins to close the gap further as V1 slightly decelerates to 85 km/h to safely negotiate the curve. The speed difference between V2 (still at 105 km/h) and V1 becomes significant, forcing V2 into a rapid response. Instead of braking sufficiently on the wet surface, V2 performs an illegal evasive maneuver by abruptly steering right toward lane 1, attempting to bypass V1 using the wide shoulder area.

This sudden lateral movement forces V4, which is traveling steadily in lane 1 at 90 km/h, to react immediately. To avoid a side collision with V2 encroaching into its lane, V4 brakes sharply, reducing speed to 60 km/h. The wet surface increases stopping distance, causing slight instability in V4’s trajectory. Meanwhile, V3 in lane 3 observes V2’s abrupt maneuver and the developing instability in adjacent lanes. To avoid potential conflict, V3 decelerates further to 60 km/h.

However, V2’s evasive action is poorly controlled due to the wet surface. While attempting to pass between V1 and V4, V2 partially loses lateral stability. Its rear begins to slip slightly, preventing precise alignment within lane 1. As V2 struggles to stabilize, it continues forward at approximately 90 km/h but cannot fully clear V1 or maintain a safe lateral gap from V4.

(Result)
The sequence culminates when V2’s unstable trajectory causes it to sideswipe V4 in lane 1. This is the first collision, involving V2 and V4, triggered by the combination of close following, large speed difference, illegal evasive maneuver, and reduced friction from the wet road surface.
